data.one_liner: Decouple Flutter layout size from hit-test size to deliver taps outside parent bounds.
data.what_it_does: Separates paint and layout size from hit size in Flutter, allowing widgets to stay visually small while having a larger tap target. Delivers pointer events that fall outside a widget's layout box using a higher-level scope.
use_when: You need a control to stay visually small like an icon or 1px edge but meet a comfortable touch target size.
You need to handle taps on elements that overflow their parent bounds without breaking neighboring layouts.
avoid_when: You have hundreds of deferred targets nested under one huge root scope, which can impact performance.
Standard padding or sizing solutions are sufficient and do not cause layout crowding.
strengths: Enables precise separation of paint/layout bounds from hit-test bounds.
Includes a built-in Dart DevTools extension for inspecting hit scopes and debugging missed taps.
Supports slivers via SliverHitScope for custom scroll views.
weaknesses: Deferred hit-testing is O(n) over registered targets on a scope, meaning large numbers of targets can affect performance.
Requires careful scope placement so that the HitScope's layout box actually covers the expanded hit area.
data.minimal_example:
HitScope(
  child: Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
    child: HitLayer(
      alignment: Alignment.center,
      behavior: HitTestBehavior.deferToChild,
      hitChild: GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onTap: () {},
        child: const SizedBox(width: 48, height: 48),
      ),
      paintChild: const IgnorePointer(
        child: Icon(Icons.add, size: 24),
      ),
    ),
  ),
)
